references.text: The preceding verse that introduces the breastpiece (חֹשֶׁן) whose dimensions are described in verse 16
Parallel text describing the construction of the breastpiece with identical measurements: square, double, a span long and a span wide
Describes how the Urim and Tummim were to be placed in the breastpiece, explaining why it was double (כָּפוּל) - to form a pocket
Ezekiel's vision of the altar also uses a square shape (רָבוּעַ) as a pattern for holy objects
The Most Holy Place in Solomon's temple was also square, showing the significance of this shape in sacred architecture
The new Jerusalem is described as square (τετράγωνος), linking back to the square holy objects in the tabernacle
